parts.title: Campus Conversation: Changing a Class Schedule
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and an academic advisor.
Student
Hello. I would like to change my schedule, if that is possible.
Advisor
Of course. What seems to be the problem?
Student
My chemistry class starts at eight in the morning, and I work at the campus cafe until midnight. I am always too tired to pay attention.
Advisor
I understand. Let me check the system. There is another chemistry section on Tuesdays and Thursdays at two in the afternoon.
Student
That would be much better. But is there still space? I heard it fills up quickly.
Advisor
There are three seats left. However, you must drop the morning section first, and the deadline to do that is this Friday.
Student
Okay. Do I need a signature from my professor?
Advisor
No, you only need to fill out this online form. It takes about five minutes. After that, you will get an email confirming the change.
Student
Great. Thank you. I will do it right after this meeting.
Advisor
One more thing. The afternoon section has a lab on Wednesdays. Will that be a problem with your job?
Student
No, I am free on Wednesday afternoons. That is perfect.
Narrator
Now get ready to answer the questions.

parts.title: Biology Lecture: Why We Sleep
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Professor
Today we are going to talk about sleep. Everyone knows that we feel bad without it, but why do humans actually need sleep? Scientists have found several answers.
Professor
First, sleep helps the body repair itself. During deep sleep, the body releases a hormone that helps muscles and other tissues grow and heal. That is why doctors often tell sick people to rest.
Professor

Second, and this is the part I find most interesting, sleep helps the brain with memory. While you sleep, your brain reviews what you learned during the day. It keeps the important information and removes things that are not useful.
Professor

In one experiment, two groups of students studied the same list of words. One group slept for eight hours, and the other group stayed awake all night. The next day, the students who slept remembered about forty percent more words.
Professor

So, what does this mean for you? Many students stay up all night before an exam. But a better plan is to study earlier and then get a full night of sleep. Think of sleep as part of studying, not as a waste of time.
Professor
Third, sleep affects our mood. People who sleep less than six hours often feel angry or sad more easily. Their attention is also weaker, which can make driving dangerous.
Professor
On Thursday, we will discuss what happens when people sleep too much. Please read the article on the course website before class.
Narrator
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Narrator
Listen again to part of the lecture.

Narrator
